## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13352>)

AgentDojo provides an extensible environment for testing whether tool-using agents complete legitimate tasks while resisting instructions embedded in untrusted tool results. It makes the security-versus-utility tradeoff measurable and supplies reusable tasks, attack surfaces, and defense baselines for agent evaluations.

**Published:** 2024-06-19 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Prompt Injection, Evaluation, Tool Use

**Positioning:** open-reference

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13352>) · [Code](<https://github.com/ethz-spylab/agentdojo>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The paper defines user and attacker goals across 97 tasks and 629 security test cases and evaluates defenses, including tool filtering. The accessible repository supports extension; arXiv records June 19, 2024 for v1 and November 24, 2024 for the inspected v3.

**Limitations:** The original scores concern historical models and the included environments, not current deployment security. Tool filtering can fail when required tools also enable an attack; the original suite does not cover continuing user tasks with an unreset context.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Failure-Transparent Agents: Benchmarking Post-Failure Reporting in Tool-Using Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35732>)

Failure-Transparent Agents isolates a reporting problem by giving models fixed failed-tool traces and checking whether subsequent claims are supported by the available evidence. Its structured evidence contract offers a concrete design to test when reducing false completion claims, while preserving useful recovery advice.

**Published:** 2026-09-28 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Evaluation, Reliability, Evidence

**Positioning:** frontier-research

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35732>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The benchmark includes 100 synthetic blocked tasks and 3,600 human-annotated responses across six models; authors report pooled false-success rates of 22.8% for baseline and 0.8% with the contract. Submission history verifies September 28, 2026 at 17:51:41 UTC.

**Limitations:** A new preprint measuring response fidelity after fixed failures, not end-to-end execution or recovery. The contract bundles multiple changes, the additional model cohort is post-confirmatory, and independent double annotation or inter-annotator agreement is not reported.
